title: Diagnostic: Type Annotation Mismatch
hints: Swift is strict about types, even for literals.
Annotate the constant as `Int` but give it a string literal.
jsBridge: TS would also flag `let score: number = "100"`, so the idea is familiar. Swift goes further: there's no `any` escape hatch by default and no implicit conversion at runtime, and type errors are always compile errors.

compass.q: TS has `as any` to silence this. What's the closest Swift escape hatch, and why is it much rarer?
Annotation mismatch vs failed `as!` cast: compile-time vs runtime. Which one can still crash?
Why does `let x: Double = 100` compile but `let x: Int = 100.0` doesn't?
When reading unfamiliar Swift errors, what does "cannot convert value of type…" usually mean in SwiftUI code?
